title: DNS Security Events
exclusions: Covers DNS through Secure Access or Umbrella only, and only blocks. Allowed queries to domains that become malicious later need a retrospective lookup against threat intelligence.
evidence: Saved alert results per identity with domains and categories, plus the endpoint investigation ticket for each command-and-control or malware hit.

controlTest.positiveScenario: From a test client protected by Umbrella or Secure Access, resolve Cisco's documented test domain `examplemalwaredomain.com`. After the next S3 sync the search returns a row for the client's identity with a Malware category.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Resolve `www.cisco.com` from the same client. The query is logged as Allowed and the search returns no row for it.

dataSources: `index=sse sourcetype=cisco:cloud_security:dns` (or `cisco:umbrella:dns` on older Umbrella exports) from the Secure Access or Umbrella S3 log bucket, read by the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569). One event per DNS query with `action`, `domain`, `category`, `blocked_category`, `identities`, and `src_ip`.
app: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7569](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7569)), which reads Cisco Secure Access and Cisco Umbrella logs from the S3 log bucket and maps the web proxy log to the CIM Web data model. The companion Cisco Secure Access App (Splunkbase 5558) adds dashboards.
spl:
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:dns", "cisco:umbrella:dns")
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="blocked"
| eval block_category=coalesce(nullif(blocked_category, ""), category)
| where match(block_category, "(?i)Malware|Command and Control|Phishing|Cryptomining|Dynamic DNS|DNS Tunneling|Newly Seen Domains|Potentially Harmful")
| stats count as blocks dc(domain) as domains values(domain) as blocked_domains values(block_category) as categories latest(_time) as last_seen by identities src_ip
| convert ctime(last_seen)
| sort - blocks
description: Lists identities and source IPs whose DNS queries Cisco Secure Access or Umbrella blocked for a security category (malware, command and control, phishing, cryptomining, dynamic DNS, DNS tunneling, newly seen domains, potentially harmful), with the domains and categories involved.
value: A security-category DNS block means a device tried to reach known-bad infrastructure. The block stopped that connection, but the device that asked is probably infected or its user clicked a phishing link, so it needs an endpoint investigation even though nothing got through.
implementation: Collect the DNS log with the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569) into `index=sse`. Schedule every 15 minutes over the last 30 minutes and alert on every identity; command-and-control blocks go to the SOC as high priority.
visualization: Alert table: identities, src_ip, blocks, domains, blocked_domains, categories, last_seen. Supporting panel: security-category blocks per day by category over 30 days (stacked column).

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Security researchers and sandboxes** — analysts and malware sandboxes resolve bad domains on purpose. Keep their identities in a lookup.

2. **Newly seen domains** — legitimate new SaaS tenants and marketing domains land in Newly Seen Domains for their first day. Treat that category as low priority unless combined with another.

**Suppression:** a lookup of research identities; throttle per identity for 4 hours.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Inputs Data Manager that reads the S3 bucket.
• Log export to Amazon S3 enabled in the Secure Access or Umbrella dashboard (Admin > Log Management), either a Cisco-managed bucket or your own, with the access key and secret for Splunk.
• An index for Secure Access and Umbrella data (this page uses `index=sse`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the network security team.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In the add-on create an S3 modular input for the DNS log path with the bucket name, region, access key, and secret, and set the index to `sse`.
• Logs reach S3 in batches, so events usually arrive in Splunk 10 to 15 minutes after the request. `action` is logged as Allowed or Blocked (ALLOWED or BLOCKED in some exports); the searches lowercase it.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:dns" | stats count by action` over 1 day and confirm both values appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:dns", "cisco:umbrella:dns")
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="blocked"
| eval block_category=coalesce(nullif(blocked_category, ""), category)
| where match(block_category, "(?i)Malware|Command and Control|Phishing|Cryptomining|Dynamic DNS|DNS Tunneling|Newly Seen Domains|Potentially Harmful")
| stats count as blocks dc(domain) as domains values(domain) as blocked_domains values(block_category) as categories latest(_time) as last_seen by identities src_ip
| convert ctime(last_seen)
| sort - blocks
```

Understanding this SPL
• The first line reads DNS logs from the current Secure Access source type and the older Umbrella one; `lower(action)` handles either case.
• `block_category` prefers the category that triggered the block; the `match` keeps only Umbrella security categories, so content-policy blocks are left out.
• `stats` by identity and source IP gives one row per device or user with every bad domain it asked for.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Access dashboard (or the Umbrella dashboard) under Reporting > Security Activity for the same time range: identities listed there should appear here.
• Spot-check one domain in Activity Search and confirm the category and identity match.
• Run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:dns" | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days; gaps longer than an hour point to S3 input failures.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 15 minutes over the last 30 minutes and throttle on `identities` for 4 hours.
• Route Command and Control and Malware rows to the SOC as high priority with an endpoint investigation; route Phishing rows to the email security team as well.
• Send to Enterprise Security as a finding with the identity as the risk object when ES is in use.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No DNS events and S3 access errors (403 AccessDenied) in the add-on log: the access key cannot read the bucket or the region is wrong.
• Categories never match: the export carries category IDs instead of names. Check `category` on one raw event and update the `match` list.
• `identities` is empty: the deployment is network-only without roaming clients or AD integration, so only `src_ip` identifies the client.
grandmaExplanation: We alert when a computer tries to look up a known dangerous website address, because that computer may be infected even though the filter stopped it.
